explanations: On a failed install, recordResult changes the device object it read (failures, lastError, status, targetVersion) but only calls save() when the device reaches the quarantine threshold. Against a fake that hands out the stored objects themselves, those changes land in the "database" anyway, so the bug never showed. The real registry returns snapshots, so the failure count is thrown away: every failure starts again from 0, the device never reaches 3, and it stays "updating". The fix saves the device on every failure path. More generally, fakes should copy on read and write, like the real dependency, so that code which relies on aliasing fails in tests.
